What to look for -- microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler#8732

#8732 reports a SILENT miscompile: under -fspv-use-descriptor-heap a variable
holding a bound resource on one path and a ResourceDescriptorHeap descriptor on
another has ALL its uses re-lowered through the heap, dropping the bound
resource from the module. That lowering lives in PR #8517, which is NOT merged.
So do not read a clean compile here as "fixed" -- and do not read the errors
below as the reported bug either. Three panes, three different things:

  1. DXC 1.9.2607 (newest release that knows the flag) -- FAILS, loudly:
       fatal error: generated SPIR-V is invalid:
       [VUID-StandaloneSpirv-OpTypeImage-06924] Cannot store to OpTypeImage...
     Interlocked* needs OpImageTexelPointer, which needs a pointer to an image
     VARIABLE; a heap descriptor is an SSA value, so DXC stores it into a
     Function image variable, and storing to an image object is illegal SPIR-V.
     Every release before 1.9.2607 answers "Unknown argument" instead.

  2. DXC trunk, same arguments -- same failure. Nothing silent is happening.

  3. DXC trunk with -Vd (validation off) -- this is the evidence pane. Read the
     disassembly and check that "%boundTex = OpVariable" is still there, that
     both descriptors are stored into the same "OpVariable ... Function" image
     variable, and that OpImageTexelPointer takes THAT variable, not the
     OpUntypedAccessChainKHR. Last store wins, so trunk's module is
     semantically what the shader asked for. It is only illegal, not wrong.

CE runs Release builds and cannot show a Debug-only assert; it also cannot show
the reported defect at all, because the code that would cause it is unmerged.
